A dot joins a line to make a vowel.
Flat vowels sit under the first sound; standing vowels sit on its right.

lines.master:
A vowel is a line with a dot joined to it.
A flat vowel tucks beneath the first sound; a standing one keeps to its right.
A sound at the bottom borrows the letters of the first sounds.
We write downwards, from top to bottom, and the first column is on the right.

lines.rookie: Use the copied scrap, Sora's board and Bun-i's note.
lines.junior: Use the copied scrap, Sora's board and Bun-i's note.
lines.master: You have the copied scrap, Sora's board and Bun-i's note.

lines.rookie: The King believes you!
lines.junior: The King believes you!
lines.master: The King is convinced!

lines.rookie: Guards open the book hall. Servants hold oiled paper over the hole.
lines.junior: The guards open the book hall. Servants hold oiled paper over the hole.
lines.master: Guards open the book hall while servants stretch oiled paper over the hole.

lines.rookie: Everyone carries the books out of the rain.
lines.junior: Everyone helps carry the books out of the rain.
lines.master: Everyone carries the books to safety, out of the rain.

lines.rookie: "You learned my letters in one night," says the King. "And Bun-i spoke to me with them."
lines.junior: "You learned my letters in a single night," says the King. "And Bun-i spoke to me with them."
lines.master: "You learned my letters in a single night," the King says, "and Bun-i reached me with them."

lines.rookie: "That is why I made them."
lines.junior: "That is why I created them."
lines.master: "That is the very reason I made them."

lines.rookie: At dawn, Bun-i comes back with her water bucket.
lines.junior: At dawn, Bun-i returns with her water bucket.
lines.master: At dawn, Bun-i returns, her water bucket in hand.

lines.rookie: The King read my letter? My very first letter?
lines.junior: The King read my letter? The very first letter I ever wrote?
lines.master: The King read my letter? The very first one I ever wrote?

lines.rookie: He did. And he says thank you.
lines.junior: He did. And he wants to say thank you.
lines.master: He did, and he sends you his thanks.

lines.rookie: Show the King who wrote the paper, and what it says.
lines.junior: Show the King who wrote the paper, and what it says.
lines.master: Prove to the King who wrote the paper and what it says.

lines.rookie: Only a few people in the palace know my letters.
lines.junior: Only a few people in the palace know my letters.
lines.master: Barely a handful in this palace know my letters.

lines.rookie: Then let me show you, Your Majesty.
lines.junior: Then let me show you, Your Majesty.
lines.master: Then allow me to show you, Your Majesty.

lines.rookie: Why did you make the letters?
lines.junior: Why did you create the letters?
lines.master: Why did you devise the letters?

lines.rookie: Many people could not write what they meant.
lines.junior: Many people could not write down what they meant.
lines.master: Too many of my people could not write what they meant.

lines.rookie: I want everyone to learn them easily.
lines.junior: I want everyone to learn them with ease.
lines.master: I want everyone to learn them with ease.

lines.rookie: The King asks: "Who wrote this?"
lines.junior: The King asks: "Who wrote this?"
lines.master: The King asks: "Who wrote this?"

lines.rookie: Bun-i, a water-carrier. She cannot write Chinese characters.
lines.junior: Bun-i, a water-carrier. She cannot write Chinese characters.
lines.master: Bun-i, who carries water. Chinese characters are beyond her.

lines.rookie: She tried the characters on my gate first.
lines.junior: So she tried the characters on my gate first.
lines.master: So she reached for the characters on my gate.

lines.rookie: That does not show who wrote it.
lines.junior: That does not show who wrote it.
lines.master: That tells me nothing of who wrote it.

lines.rookie: The copied scrap shows the writer could not write Chinese characters.
lines.junior: The copied scrap shows that the writer could not write Chinese characters.
lines.master: The copied scrap shows the writer could not write Chinese characters.

lines.rookie: The King asks: "How can she write after only ten days?"
lines.junior: The King asks: "How can she write after only ten days of lessons?"
lines.master: The King asks: "How could she write after a mere ten days?"

lines.rookie: Your letters copy the mouth. They are easy to learn.
lines.junior: Your letters copy the mouth, so they are easy to learn.
lines.master: Your letters copy the mouth: they are simple to learn.

lines.rookie: Then my scholar was right. Ten days are enough.
lines.junior: Then my scholar was right: ten days are enough.
lines.master: Then my scholar was right. Ten days suffice.

lines.rookie: That does not show how she learned.
lines.junior: That does not show how she learned.
lines.master: That does not explain how she learned.

lines.rookie: Sora's board shows how the letters are made.
lines.junior: Sora's board shows how the letters are made.
lines.master: Sora's board shows how the letters are built.

lines.rookie: The King asks: "And you read it in one night?"
lines.junior: The King asks: "And you read it in a single night?"
lines.master: The King asks: "And you read it in a single night?"

lines.rookie: Bun-i wrote "the book hall roof". There is a hole in it.
lines.junior: Bun-i wrote "the book hall roof". There is a hole in it.
lines.master: Bun-i wrote "the book hall roof": there is a hole in it.

lines.rookie: The book hall roof! Open the book hall!
lines.junior: The roof of the book hall! Open the book hall!
lines.master: The book hall roof! Open the book hall at once!

lines.rookie: That does not say what she wrote.
lines.junior: That does not say what she wrote.
lines.master: That does not tell me what she wrote.

lines.rookie: Bun-i's note names the book hall roof.
lines.junior: Bun-i's note names the roof of the book hall.
lines.master: Bun-i's note names the roof of the book hall.

lines.rookie: CLOSE THE CASE
lines.junior: CLOSE THE CASE
lines.master: CLOSE THE CASE
